headline_marked: Govt says [[Shakib Al Hasan has no scope to return]] to Bangladesh
headline: Govt says Shakib Al Hasan has no scope to return to Bangladesh
summary: State Minister for Youth and Sports Aminul Haque says the cricketer's participation in an event with ousted PM Sheikh Hasina has closed the door on his return.
details: Bangladesh's most successful cricketer, Shakib Al Hasan, now faces a bleak future regarding his return to the country. State Minister for Youth and Sports Aminul Haque stated that there is no longer any room for flexibility or tolerance toward the cricketer.
The decision follows Shakib's participation via telephone from Sri Lanka in a media event in New Delhi where ousted former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina addressed journalists.
Shakib, a former lawmaker for the Awami League, is currently among dozens facing murder investigations related to a deadly police crackdown on protesters that toppled the previous government.
Minister Haque emphasized that anyone who has 'taken the stage with the autocrat' no longer has the opportunity to return to Bangladesh.
Despite the Bangladesh Cricket Board's earlier indication in January that he could play again, this recent alignment with the fugitive former PM has sparked widespread anger.
Shakib, who has played over 400 international matches and represented Bangladesh at five World Cups, had previously announced retirement plans in September 2024.
caption:
No way back? The government says Shakib Al Hasan has lost his chance to return to Bangladesh after appearing in an event with Sheikh Hasina.

Bangladesh's most successful cricketer, Shakib Al Hasan, now faces a bleak future regarding his return to the country. State Minister for Youth and Sports Aminul Haque stated that there is no longer any room for flexibility or tolerance toward the cricketer.

The decision follows Shakib's participation via telephone from Sri Lanka in a media event in New Delhi where ousted former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina addressed journalists.

Shakib, a former lawmaker for the Awami League, is currently among dozens facing murder investigations related to a deadly police crackdown on protesters that toppled the previous government.

Minister Haque emphasized that anyone who has 'taken the stage with the autocrat' no longer has the opportunity to return to Bangladesh.

Despite the Bangladesh Cricket Board's earlier indication in January that he could play again, this recent alignment with the fugitive former PM has sparked widespread anger.

Shakib, who has played over 400 international matches and represented Bangladesh at five World Cups, had previously announced retirement plans in September 2024.

headline_marked: Police warn of [[coordinated propaganda campaign targeting senior officers]]
headline: Police warn of coordinated propaganda campaign targeting senior officers
summary: Bangladesh Police threaten strict legal action against those spreading fabricated information to destabilize law and order and tarnish government image.
details: Bangladesh Police have warned of strict legal action against individuals spreading false, fabricated, and provocative propaganda on social media targeting senior police officers and key government figures.
Police Headquarters alleged that a systematic disinformation campaign is being run on platforms like Facebook to create public confusion, destabilize law and order, and undermine police morale.
The authorities claim the campaign intensified after law enforcement increased legal action against banned political parties and refused to yield to undue lobbying.
It is further alleged that some frustrated individuals, denied their lobbying requests, have resorted to spreading fabricated information to tarnish the government's image.
Police Headquarters claimed to have evidence that some of these propagandists are accused in various criminal offenses and have even demanded money to stop the propaganda.
The public is urged not to believe, share, or circulate misleading content and to help prevent the spread of rumors and disinformation.
caption:
Police warn of a systematic smear campaign targeting senior officers and government figures. Legal action is now imminent.

Bangladesh Police have warned of strict legal action against individuals spreading false, fabricated, and provocative propaganda on social media targeting senior police officers and key government figures.

Police Headquarters alleged that a systematic disinformation campaign is being run on platforms like Facebook to create public confusion, destabilize law and order, and undermine police morale.

The authorities claim the campaign intensified after law enforcement increased legal action against banned political parties and refused to yield to undue lobbying.

It is further alleged that some frustrated individuals, denied their lobbying requests, have resorted to spreading fabricated information to tarnish the government's image.

Police Headquarters claimed to have evidence that some of these propagandists are accused in various criminal offenses and have even demanded money to stop the propaganda.

The public is urged not to believe, share, or circulate misleading content and to help prevent the spread of rumors and disinformation.
